options.B: The deceased's illegitimate child, treated as legitimate
options.C: A former employer with no insurable interest
options.D: A neighbour who arranged the funeral

explanation: Proper claimants include the executors, spouse, child, parent, sibling or relatives, and an illegitimate child is treated as legitimate. A creditor without an assignment or a neighbour is not a proper claimant.

stem: Under section 61(2), what is the maximum amount an insurer may advance without a Grant of Probate or Letter of Administration?
explanation: The no-probate advance limit is $150,000. Larger amounts require a Grant of Probate or Letter of Administration before payment.

stem: Under a joint tenancy, on the death of one owner the deceased's share:

options.A: Passes to the deceased's own estate and beneficiaries
options.B: Is paid to the Government
options.C: Is frozen until probate is granted
options.D: Passes to the surviving tenant(s)

explanation: Under joint tenancy the share passes to the surviving tenant(s), which is why joint-life policies are usually written this way. Passing to the deceased's own estate describes tenancy in common instead.

stem: Proof of age is required in a death claim only when:

options.A: Age was not admitted when the policy was issued
options.B: The policy was assigned
options.C: The claim exceeds $150,000
options.D: The deceased died overseas

explanation: Proof of age (NRIC or birth certificate) is needed only if age was not admitted at inception. If age was already admitted when the policy was issued, this proof is unnecessary.

stem: The deceased left a valid Will. Who proves title to the policy proceeds and with what document?

options.A: An administrator with a Letter of Administration
options.B: An executor with a Grant of Probate
options.C: The assignee with the deed of assignment
options.D: The nominee with a statutory declaration

explanation: Where there is a Will, an executor proves title with a Grant of Probate. An administrator with a Letter of Administration is the route only when there is no Will.

stem: A person has been missing without trace for over seven years. Regarding the statutory presumption of death:

options.A: The court's presumption automatically binds the insurer to pay
options.B: The presumption requires only 3 years of absence
options.C: A presumption may be sought after 7 years, but it does not bind the insurer, which can make its own enquiries
options.D: The insurer must pay double the sum assured

explanation: A presumption of death needs 7 or more years missing and can be sought from the court, but it does not bind the insurer, which may make its own enquiries. The court presumption is not automatically conclusive against the insurer.

stem: For a Pure Endowment maturity claim, what must be established?

options.A: Proof that the insured has died
options.B: A Grant of Probate
options.C: Consent of all nominees
options.D: Proof that the insured survived to maturity

explanation: A Pure Endowment maturity claim requires proof the insured survived to maturity, since it pays only on survival. Proof of death is relevant to a death claim, not a Pure Endowment maturity.

stem: The LIA Register of Unclaimed Proceeds allows the public to search for proceeds unclaimed for more than:

options.A: 12 months
options.B: 3 months
options.C: 6 months
options.D: 24 months

explanation: Launched on 4 January 2016, the register lets the public search for death or maturity proceeds unclaimed for more than 12 months, and it is updated every 6 months. The 6-month figure is the update cycle, not the unclaimed threshold.

stem: A contract that one party may choose to set aside but which remains in force until then is described as:

options.A: Void
options.B: Voidable
options.C: Valid and irrevocable
options.D: Illegal

explanation: A voidable contract stands until the innocent party chooses to avoid it. A void contract, by contrast, never had legal existence at all.

stem: In a life insurance contract, which of the following constitutes the offer?

options.A: The insurer's advertisement of the product
options.B: The insurer issuing the policy document
options.C: The proposal form together with the first premium
options.D: The adviser's illustration of benefits

explanation: The proposal form plus first premium is the offer; the insurer issuing the policy is the acceptance. An advertisement is only an invitation to treat, not an offer.

stem: A 15-year-old wishes to take out an insurance policy. Which statement is correct?

options.A: A person under 10 may contract freely
options.B: A minor can assign and surrender a policy at any age
options.C: No one under 21 may hold any insurance policy
options.D: A person over 10 may contract, but under 16 needs written parental consent; a minor cannot assign or surrender until 18

explanation: A person over 10 can enter an insurance contract, but under 16 needs written parental consent, and a minor cannot assign, mortgage, surrender or give valid discharge until 18. A minor cannot freely assign or surrender.

stem: Insurance contracts are governed by uberrima fides rather than caveat emptor because:

options.A: Only the proposer knows their own risks, so utmost good faith is required from both parties
options.B: The insurer alone knows the full risk
options.C: Insurance is a form of gambling
options.D: The buyer is always at fault for non-disclosure

explanation: Insurance uses uberrima fides (utmost good faith) because only the proposer knows their own risks, and the duty binds both parties. Ordinary sales use caveat emptor (buyer beware), which is inadequate here.

stem: How is the materiality of a fact judged for the purposes of disclosure?

options.A: By the applicant's honest opinion of what matters
options.B: Objectively, by whether it would influence a prudent insurer
options.C: By whether the adviser thought it relevant
options.D: By industry custom alone

explanation: Materiality is judged objectively by the prudent-insurer test, so the insured's honest belief that a fact was immaterial does not excuse non-disclosure. The misrepresentation must also have induced the insurer to contract.

stem: Regarding the basis clause, which statement reflects the current LIA position?

options.A: It is freely allowed on all policies
options.B: It has been abolished for every policy type
options.C: It is no longer allowed on the owner's OWN life, though it remains valid for 'life of another' policies
options.D: It turns all answers into representations, not warranties

explanation: The LIA no longer allows a basis clause on the owner's own life, though it remains valid for 'life of another' policies. A basis clause actually turns proposal answers into warranties, not representations.

stem: The section 25(5) warning on a proposal form informs the proposer that:

options.A: Premiums are non-refundable after the free-look period
options.B: The policy cannot be assigned without consent
options.C: Claims must be made within 12 months
options.D: Non-disclosure of facts known or ought to be known may mean nothing is payable and the contract can be voided from inception

explanation: The section 25(5) warning must prominently state that non-disclosure of facts known or ought to be known may mean nothing is payable, letting the insurer declare the contract void from inception. It concerns disclosure, not free-look refunds.

stem: Where a question in a proposal form is genuinely ambiguous, the contra proferentem rule means it is construed:

options.A: Against the insurer who drafted it, so doubt favours the insured
options.B: In favour of the insurer who drafted it
options.C: According to the adviser's interpretation
options.D: As void for uncertainty

explanation: Contra proferentem construes an ambiguous question against the drafter (the insurer), so doubt favours the insured. It does not favour the insurer, nor does it void the term.

stem: In the case of innocent non-disclosure of a material fact, what is the correct outcome?

options.A: The insurer avoids the contract and keeps the premium
options.B: The insurer avoids the contract ab initio but must return the premium
options.C: The insurer pays the claim in full and keeps the premium
options.D: The insurer may claim damages

explanation: Innocent non-disclosure lets the insurer avoid ab initio if material, but the premium must be returned. The insurer keeps premiums only where there was fraud.

stem: Which set of vitiating factors renders a contract VOIDABLE (rather than void)?

options.A: Illegality and mistake
options.B: Lack of insurable interest and illegality
options.C: Misrepresentation, duress and undue influence
options.D: Non est factum and mistake

explanation: Misrepresentation, duress and undue influence make a contract voidable at the innocent party's choice. Illegality and mistake make it void, and a policy without insurable interest is a void wagering contract.

stem: The intentional and voluntary relinquishment of a known right, whether express or by conduct, is called:

options.A: Estoppel
options.B: Ratification
options.C: Rescission
options.D: Waiver

explanation: Waiver is the intentional, voluntary relinquishment of a known right. Estoppel is different: it arises when a party creates an impression, an innocent party relies and suffers, and the insurer is then barred from denying it.

stem: A policyholder understated his age at inception. On discovery, how is the benefit adjusted?

options.A: The sum assured is reduced to what the premium would have bought at his true age
options.B: The excess premium is refunded with interest
options.C: The policy is voided from inception
options.D: The premium is increased retroactively with a penalty

explanation: Understated age reduces the sum assured to what the premium would have bought at the true age. Overstated age, by contrast, refunds the excess premium without interest.

stem: A life insured dies by suicide 18 months after the policy was issued, with a one-year suicide clause. What is the outcome?

options.A: The policy is void and premiums are refunded without interest
options.B: The claim is paid, since the death occurred after the suicide period
options.C: Nothing is payable because suicide is always excluded
options.D: Only the cash value is paid

explanation: Suicide after the specified period (usually 1 year) is paid, sane or insane. Voiding and refunding premiums applies only where suicide occurs within the suicide period.

stem: Non-forfeiture options that prevent lapse for non-payment apply to:

options.A: All policies including ILPs
options.B: Term policies only
options.C: Cash-value traditional policies only, not ILPs
options.D: Group insurance only

explanation: Non-forfeiture options apply to cash-value traditional policies only, never to ILPs; such a policy in force over 3 years will not lapse for non-payment. ILPs are expressly excluded from these options.

stem: As an agent of the insurer, an adviser owes a fiduciary duty that means he must:

options.A: Maximise his own commission
options.B: Follow only the client's instructions
options.C: Guarantee the policy's investment returns
options.D: Act in the principal's best interest

explanation: An agent is a fiduciary who must act in the principal's (insurer's) best interest, and life agents are legally 'representatives' under the FAA. Maximising personal commission would breach the fiduciary duty.

stem: Under the Insurance Act, the agency agreement between an insurer and its agent must be:

options.A: In writing
options.B: Oral and confirmed by conduct
options.C: Implied from the parties' dealings
options.D: Registered with the court

explanation: The Insurance Act requires the insurer-agent agreement to be in writing. While agency can arise by implication or by operation of law generally, this particular relationship must be a written agreement.

stem: Which of the following is a FIDUCIARY duty of an agent (as distinct from a common-law duty)?

options.A: To exercise due care and skill
options.B: To avoid conflicts of interest and take no secret commissions
options.C: To account for and separate money received
options.D: To inform the principal of material facts

explanation: Avoiding conflicts of interest, not delegating authority, and taking no bribes or secret commissions are fiduciary duties. Exercising due care and skill and accounting for money are common-law duties.

stem: Under the dual-agency rule, an intermediary acts as agent of the INSURED when:

options.A: Collecting premiums on the insurer's behalf
options.B: Issuing a cover note
options.C: Advising on the cover required and completing (but not signing) the proposal form
options.D: Acting under delegated authority from the insurer

explanation: Advising on cover required and completing (but not signing) the proposal form makes the intermediary the insured's agent. Collecting premiums or issuing a cover note make him the insurer's agent.

stem: Apparent (ostensible) authority arises based on:

options.A: The agent's own representations about his powers
options.B: A written clause in the agency contract
options.C: Whatever is necessary to carry out express authority
options.D: The principal's conduct leading a third party reasonably to believe authority exists

explanation: Apparent authority rests on the principal's conduct, not the agent's, and binds the insurer to transactions made under it. Authority necessary to carry out express authority describes implied authority instead.

stem: Under usual authority, an agent may explain proposal questions and policy terms but CANNOT:

options.A: Enter, renew or revive a contract, vary terms, or waive conditions
options.B: Describe the product's benefits
options.C: Answer a client's questions about exclusions
options.D: Provide a benefit illustration

explanation: Usual authority explains but cannot bind: an agent cannot enter, renew or revive a contract, vary terms, or waive conditions. Explaining terms and providing illustrations are within usual authority.

stem: When an agent acts outside his authority, which of the following is true?

options.A: The principal is always bound to the third party
options.B: The principal is not bound, but the agent may incur personal liability
options.C: The agent automatically retains full commission
options.D: The contract is void for illegality

explanation: If an agent acts outside authority the principal is not bound, but the agent can incur personal liability, and indemnity is lost if the act was unauthorised. The principal is not automatically bound.

stem: A principal ratifies an unauthorised act done by his agent. From what date does ratification take effect?

options.A: The date the principal signs the ratification
options.B: The date the third party is notified
options.C: The date of the agent's original act
options.D: The date the policy is issued

explanation: Ratification takes effect from the date of the agent's act, not the date of ratification, and it must cover the whole deal. Note too that an undisclosed principal cannot ratify.

stem: Which of the following terminates an agency by operation of law?

options.A: Revocation by the principal
options.B: Renunciation by the agent
options.C: A dispute over commission
options.D: Death, bankruptcy or unsoundness of mind of either party

explanation: Termination by operation of law includes expiry of agreed time, complete performance, frustration or illegality, and death, bankruptcy, disability or unsoundness of mind of either party. Revocation and renunciation are terminations by the parties, not by operation of law.

stem: Which of the following is NOT taxable as income in Singapore?

options.A: A capital gain on the sale of shares
options.B: Employment salary derived in Singapore
options.C: Rental income received in Singapore
options.D: Trade profits accruing in Singapore

explanation: Singapore has no capital gains tax, and gifts, legacies and lottery winnings are not income. Salary, rental income and trade profits are all taxable income.

stem: In the income tax funnel, Chargeable Income is arrived at by taking:

options.A: Statutory income less allowable expenses only
options.B: Assessable income less personal reliefs
options.C: Assessable income plus approved donations
options.D: Statutory income plus personal reliefs

explanation: Chargeable Income equals assessable income less personal reliefs and is what is taxed. Deducting allowable expenses and donations from statutory income gets you only as far as assessable income.

stem: A resident individual has chargeable income of $18,000. How is this taxed?

options.A: At a flat 15%
options.B: At the top rate of 22%
options.C: No tax is payable, as chargeable income is $20,000 or below
options.D: At 2% on the full amount

explanation: Resident rates are progressive from 2% to 22%, with no tax if chargeable income is $20,000 or below, so $18,000 attracts no tax. The flat 15% applies to non-residents, not residents.

stem: To claim Qualifying Child Relief, the child must be unmarried, under 16 (or studying full-time), and earning under:
explanation: Qualifying Child Relief requires the child to be unmarried, under 16 or studying full-time, and earning under $4,000. Foreign Maid Levy Relief, by contrast, is twice the levy paid.

stem: A taxpayer's total CPF contribution in the previous year was $5,000. Can he claim life insurance relief?

options.A: No, because his CPF contribution is $5,000 or more, exhausting the combined cap
options.B: Yes, up to 7% of the sum assured
options.C: Yes, up to the full premiums paid
options.D: Yes, but only half the premium

explanation: A taxpayer is not eligible for life insurance relief if total CPF contributions are $5,000 or more, since the relief shares a combined $5,000 cap with CPF relief. Only where CPF is below $5,000 can the relief be claimed.

stem: Who tends to benefit MOST from life insurance relief?

options.A: Salaried employees whose CPF already hits $5,000
options.B: The self-employed with no voluntary CPF, and foreigners exempt from CPF
options.C: Retirees drawing CPF LIFE payouts
options.D: Undischarged bankrupts

explanation: The self-employed with no voluntary CPF and foreigners exempt from CPF benefit most, because their CPF is not already using up the $5,000 cap. Employees whose CPF already hits $5,000 get no life insurance relief.

stem: SRS contribution relief for a Singapore citizen or PR is capped at what percentage of the Absolute Income Base?
explanation: SRS relief is capped at 15% of the Absolute Income Base for a citizen or PR, and 35% for a foreigner. The AIB is 17 months of the CPF salary ceiling.

stem: What is the key difference between a tax relief and a tax rebate?

options.A: A relief reduces the tax payable; a rebate reduces chargeable income
options.B: Both reduce chargeable income equally
options.C: Both reduce the tax payable equally
options.D: A relief reduces chargeable income; a rebate reduces the tax payable

explanation: A relief reduces chargeable income, while a rebate reduces the tax payable directly. The Parenthood Tax Rebate, for example, offsets tax at $5k, $10k and $20k for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd-plus child.

stem: An SRS member withdraws funds BEFORE the statutory retirement age. What is the tax treatment?

options.A: The full amount is 100% taxed plus a 5% penalty
options.B: Only 50% is taxed, with no penalty
options.C: The withdrawal is entirely tax-free
options.D: Only the investment gains are taxed

explanation: Premature SRS withdrawal is 100% taxed plus a 5% penalty. The 50%-taxed concession applies only on or after the statutory retirement age, on death, on medical grounds, or for a foreigner holding the account 10-plus years.

stem: Under the current nomination framework, if a policy owner makes no nomination and leaves no Will, the death proceeds pass:

options.A: Automatically to the insurer
options.B: Under the Intestate Succession Act
options.C: To the adviser who sold the policy
options.D: To the first person to submit a claim

explanation: With no nomination, proceeds pass by Will, or failing that under the Intestate Succession Act. The framework offers two deliberate choices (revocable and trust) but nomination is not compulsory.

stem: The statutory nomination framework applies only to which policies, and who may nominate?

options.A: Indemnity (hospital and surgical) policies; any owner over 16
options.B: Group insurance policies; the employer
options.C: Non-indemnity policies; the nominator must be both owner and life insured, and at least 18
options.D: All policies; anyone with insurable interest

explanation: Nomination applies only to non-indemnity policies (life and personal accident with death benefits), and the nominator must be both the policy owner and the life insured, and at least 18. Indemnity policies are excluded because they reimburse the owner's own losses.

stem: Under a trust (irrevocable) nomination, which statement is correct?

options.A: The owner keeps living benefits and full control
options.B: Anyone including a corporation may be nominated
options.C: The owner may surrender freely without consent
options.D: Only spouse and/or children may be nominated, and changes need all nominees' consent

explanation: A trust nomination allows only spouse and/or children as nominees, and the owner needs the written consent of all nominees to change, revoke, take a loan or surrender. The owner loses all rights, so both living and death benefits belong to the nominees.

stem: Under a TRUST nomination, if a nominee dies before the policy owner, that nominee's share goes to:

options.A: The nominee's own estate
options.B: The surviving nominees proportionally
options.C: The policy owner
options.D: The Government

explanation: Under a trust nomination a deceased nominee's share goes to their estate. This contrasts with a revocable nomination, where the deceased nominee's share is redistributed to the surviving nominees.

stem: Under a revocable nomination, which statement is correct?

options.A: Both living and death benefits pass to the nominees
options.B: Only death benefits go to nominees; the owner keeps living benefits and full control and may change it without the nominee's consent
options.C: The owner needs the nominee's consent to revoke
options.D: An animal may be nominated

explanation: Under a revocable nomination only death benefits go to nominees, the owner keeps living benefits and full control, and can change or revoke anytime without the nominee's consent. Any legal entity except an animal may be nominated.

stem: Under a revocable nomination with several nominees, one nominee dies before the owner. What happens to that nominee's share?

options.A: The entire nomination is revoked
options.B: It passes to the deceased nominee's estate
options.C: It is redistributed proportionally to the surviving nominees
options.D: It reverts to the insurer

explanation: With multiple nominees under a revocable nomination, a deceased nominee's share is redistributed proportionally to the survivors, and the nomination is revoked only when ALL die. It does not go to the deceased nominee's estate, which is the trust-nomination rule.

stem: Which nomination is permitted on CPFIS, CPF LIFE, DPS and SRS policies?

options.A: Trust nomination only
options.B: Either revocable or trust
options.C: No nomination is allowed
options.D: Revocable nomination only

explanation: CPFIS, CPF LIFE, DPS and SRS policies allow revocable nomination only, since the money is for the member's own retirement. Group insurance, by contrast, allows no nomination at all.

stem: A policy owner makes a revocable nomination, then later writes a Will leaving 'all my property' to charity, without naming the policy. Which prevails over the proceeds?

options.A: The nomination, because a general Will does not override it without specific policy details
options.B: The Will, because it is the later document
options.C: Neither; the proceeds pass under intestacy
options.D: The proceeds are split equally

explanation: A general Will does not override a nomination; the Will must name the specific policy (insurer, policy number, proceeds). A Will covering 'all property' is not enough to displace the nomination.

stem: For a Will to be valid, the testator must generally be:

options.A: 18 or older and of sound mind, witnessed by one person
options.B: 21 or older and of sound mind, witnessed by two persons present together
options.C: Of any age if witnessed by a lawyer
options.D: A Singapore citizen only

explanation: A valid Will needs a testator 21 or older of sound mind and two witnesses present together (with a narrow exception for soldiers on active service or mariners at sea). One witness or an age of 18 is insufficient.

stem: A man dies intestate leaving a spouse and two children. How is his estate distributed under the Intestate Succession Act?

options.A: All to the spouse
options.B: One-third to the spouse, two-thirds to the children
options.C: Half to the spouse, half divided equally between the children
options.D: All divided equally among the children

explanation: With a spouse and children, half goes to the spouse and the other half is divided equally among the children. 'All to spouse' applies only where there are no children or parents.

stem: Which of the following avoids the need for probate?

options.A: A valid Will naming an executor
options.B: A testamentary trust created by the Will
options.C: Dying intestate
options.D: A trust set up during the settlor's lifetime

explanation: Only a trust (set up during the settlor's lifetime) avoids probate. A Will does not, and even a testamentary trust, which arises through the Will, does not avoid probate.

stem: A self-employed doctor makes no CPF contributions. He pays $6,000 in annual premiums on his own life policy, which has a sum assured of $60,000. What is his life insurance relief?

options.A: $4,200, being 7% of the $60,000 sum assured
options.B: $6,000, the full premium paid
options.C: $5,000, the combined CPF/life relief cap
options.D: $3,600, being 6% of the sum assured

explanation: Relief is the lowest of ($5,000 - CPF = $5,000), 7% of the sum assured ($60,000 x 7% = $4,200), and premiums paid ($6,000). The lowest is $4,200. Choosing $5,000 forgets the 7%-of-sum-assured cap, which binds here.

stem: A foreigner exempt from CPF pays $3,000 in premiums on a policy with a $100,000 sum assured. What life insurance relief can she claim?

options.A: $7,000, being 7% of the sum assured
options.B: $3,000, the premiums paid
options.C: $5,000, the combined cap
options.D: $2,000, half the cap

explanation: Relief is the lowest of ($5,000 - CPF = $5,000), 7% of $100,000 = $7,000, and premiums paid = $3,000. The lowest is the actual premium of $3,000. The 7% figure of $7,000 is not the binding limit here.

stem: A self-employed taxpayer made $2,000 of voluntary CPF contributions last year, pays $4,500 in premiums, and holds a $80,000 sum assured policy. What is his life insurance relief?

options.A: $5,600, being 7% of the sum assured
options.B: $4,500, the premiums paid
options.C: $3,000, being $5,000 less the $2,000 CPF contribution
options.D: $5,000, the full combined cap

explanation: Relief is the lowest of ($5,000 - $2,000 CPF = $3,000), 7% of $80,000 = $5,600, and premiums = $4,500. The lowest is $3,000. Forgetting to subtract the $2,000 CPF from the $5,000 cap would wrongly give $5,000.

stem: A married Singapore resident couple have their first and second Singaporean children. What is their total Parenthood Tax Rebate?
explanation: The PTR is $5,000 for the 1st child and $10,000 for the 2nd, totalling $15,000. Using $10,000 + $20,000 wrongly applies the 3rd-child rate to the 2nd child.

stem: A retiree past the statutory retirement age withdraws $40,000 from her SRS account in a single year. How much is subject to tax?

options.A: $20,000, being 50% of the withdrawal
options.B: $40,000, the full amount
options.C: $2,000, being 5% of the withdrawal
options.D: Nothing, SRS withdrawals are tax-free

explanation: Withdrawal on or after the statutory retirement age is only 50% taxed, so $40,000 x 50% = $20,000 is taxable. The full $40,000 and a 5% penalty apply only to premature withdrawals.

stem: A woman dies intestate leaving an estate of $600,000, survived by her husband and three children. How much does the husband receive?

options.A: $600,000, the whole estate
options.B: $300,000, being half the estate
options.C: $200,000, an equal one-third share
options.D: $150,000, being a quarter share

explanation: With a spouse and children, half goes to the spouse: $600,000 x 1/2 = $300,000. The remaining $300,000 is split among the three children ($100,000 each). Dividing the estate equally among all four would wrongly give $150,000.

stem: A man dies intestate with an estate of $500,000, leaving no spouse and no children, survived only by both his parents. How much does each parent receive?

options.A: $500,000 to one parent only
options.B: $166,667 each, a one-third share

explanation: With parents only and no spouse or children, all goes to the parents equally: $500,000 / 2 = $250,000 each. The half-to-spouse rule does not apply because there is no surviving spouse.

stem: A man dies intestate leaving an estate of $400,000, survived by his wife and both parents but no children. How is the estate distributed?

options.A: All $400,000 to the wife
options.B: $133,333 to the wife and each parent equally
options.C: $300,000 to the wife, $50,000 to each parent
options.D: $200,000 to the wife, $100,000 to each parent

explanation: With a spouse and parents (no children), half goes to the spouse and half is divided equally between the parents: wife $200,000, and $200,000 / 2 = $100,000 to each parent. The wife does not take the whole estate when parents survive and there are no children.
